workload.counts: 14 equally weighted timed cases plus eight unscored correctness fixtures and their changed-input/same-storage repeats
workload.preserved: Both long cases use batch 148, query length 2, heads 64/128, nominal cache length 32768, topk 16384 and page size 64. The twelve production-derived cases use all four approved configurations and batch/query pairs (2,1), (74,2), (128,3). Eight fixtures cross heads/scopes/sinks with primary (650,576,53) and optional extra (512,64,61). Scale is 512**(-0.55).
workload.transformations: The twelve primary windows end at cache_length-query_length+row+1. Other indices use the frozen native uniform-sampling helper. Physical page permutations, tensors and finite sink values vary by seed, while work profiles and sink categories are fixed. Fixture length vectors are [0,7,650,317] and [0,5,512,129]; masks are [0,topk,topk//2+1,0]; batch 2 query row 1 is entirely padded in both scopes. One valid selected token per fixture scope is zero-valued.
workload.distribution: Native BF16 clamped normal queries and clamped normal/10 caches. Length vectors use Python normalvariate as native lib.py does. Frozen topk lengths and normal sink categories are generated once with Python Random rather than device RNG, with the same distributions; they never vary privately. Cache generation is chunked into at most 1024 pages to bound temporary memory, using the frozen native padded-stride generator and MODEL1 quantizer. This changes random-number ordering, not marginal distributions, shapes, mask profiles, scale, or stored precision.
workload.poisoning: Every unselected or length-masked token, including ragged tails, is poisoned before quantization unless another row validly selects it. Unlike native lib.py's mask indexing, -1 padding is filtered before marking selected slots, so it cannot accidentally spare the final physical token.
workload.reference: Readable independent selected-byte decoding avoids full-cache dequantization and gathers only valid entries. E8M0 exponent bytes are decoded as powers of two, with 255 treated as NaN. Valid selected values must be finite, including zeros. Expected results use preserved inputs after the timed native call. Frozen native compare.py defines tolerances and zero-reference distance handling.
workload.public_private: The shared public/protected workload and runner closure is byte-identical. utils/protocol.py publishes nine fixed public seeds and derives REPETITIONS from that tuple. Both metrics and both entrypoints use it; private seeds are nine distinct samples drawn at execution. Every paired incumbent/candidate input is identical. Only values and equivalent index/page realizations differ between public and private. No case, work profile, precision, tolerance or timing boundary changed.

reference_repair.files: solution/direct_schedule.patch and solution/solve.sh; obsolete balanced_scheduler.patch removed
reference_repair.mechanism: Fuse rectangular request/split scheduling into the native attention blocks for SM100 MODEL1 uniform selection lengths or sufficiently large batches. Derive interval and split offsets arithmetically inside the measured call instead of launching a metadata kernel. Large batches use unsplit direct output, eliminating both metadata allocations, both accumulation allocations and the combine kernel; the 128-head tensor-map encoder skips its absent accumulator. Small uniform batches retain multiple disjoint splits with the native combine arithmetic. Small variable-length batches keep native scheduling. Inputs and outputs are never cached.
reference_repair.rationale: The retained profile shows allocation and launch/configuration overhead alongside a scheduler kernel. The previous balanced scan changed GPU scheduling but did not reproducibly reduce complete-call latency. This reference instead removes whole launches and unnecessary buffers; unlike the previous unsplit patch, direct metadata is computed in the attention block itself.
reference_repair.tradeoffs: One request per block or cluster changes wave balance and loses persistent cross-request scheduling. Short uniform splits may have more epilogue traffic. The 64/128-head arithmetic pipelines and packed-byte gathers remain native, leaving tensor-core scheduling, sparse loads, dequantization and cross-query reuse as deeper research directions. This is not an experimentally established speedup ceiling or proof of weeks of improvement.
